source: Tanaka, K. L. et al. (2014). Geologic Map of Mars. USGS Scientific Investigations Map 3292, scale 1:20,000,000.
attribution: USGS Astrogeology / NASA (Tanaka et al. 2014, SIM 3292)
caveats: Global 1:20M map: unit contacts are placed to within kilometres to tens of kilometres, so this is regional context, not what is under the rover's wheels.
Units are mapped from orbit (morphology, crater counts); none of these units has been visited in Arcadia Planitia.
The metres-thick ice-rich mantle seen in the HiRISE images at every site (Mustard et al. 2001) is too thin and patchy for this map; the mapped unit is what lies beneath it.
Ages are relative epochs from crater statistics, not radiometric dates.
nearest_contact_km is measured to the mapped contact; treat values under ~10 km as 'near a contact', not a precise distance.

places.description: Rugged, hummocky, pitted plains of poorly defined flows, hundreds to >1,000 km across; interpreted as lava and perhaps volcaniclastic flows. Tens of metres or more thick.

Planar to undulating plains across most of the northern lowlands; sediments from outflow channels and highland margins, likely with lavas; pervasively modified by periglaciation and mantling. Hundreds of metres to km thick.
